players.product: RockBlock modular natural-gas generator systems (designed, assembled, installed and operated turnkey with Granite software) for on-site bridge / prime and backup power at AI data centers

connects_to.relationship: on-site natural-gas resiliency power system (RockBlock generators) for a Microsoft data center in San Jose, California

contracts.signal: Prospectus: ERock's distributed power system project with Microsoft Corporation in San Jose, California is engineered to deliver 63 MW of high-availability resiliency for data center operations while also providing grid stabilization services to CAISO; the RockBlock outperformed Microsoft's standards for transient response. ERock expects to begin delivering generators to the Microsoft site in the second half of 2026; once operational the system can dispatch power with less than 15 minutes' notice by taking the data center's grid imports to zero.
contracts.type: power system project (generator supply, resiliency and grid support)

connects_to.relationship: white-label distributed generation program partner (generation equipment, installation and O&M for Entergy's Power Through resiliency customers)

contracts.signal: Prospectus: ERock has partnered with Entergy Corporation under a white label program to provide generation equipment, ESI (equipment, supply and installation) services and O&M services for Entergy's C&I customers in its Power Through resiliency services program, including hospitals, industrial operations and data centers; Entergy uses ERock's distributed generation systems to help meet its resource adequacy requirements. ERock also cites proprietary offtake and commercial arrangements with utilities such as Entergy and CPS Energy.

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Meta (via utility El Paso Electric): as part of Meta Platforms' $10 billion investment in AI data center capacity in El Paso, Texas, ERock is partnering with El Paso Electric to provide 366 MW of onsite generating capacity (the McCloud Generation Facility), comprising 163 modular RockBlocks with an initial commercial operation date targeted for mid-2027, providing multiple years of bridge power while El Paso Electric builds the McCloud East substation; once the substation is energized the facility is slated to become a grid-tied dispatchable generation facility, subject to regulatory review.
quarterly_data.figure: 366 MW; 163 RockBlocks; commercial operation targeted mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Wistron: in May 2025 ERock signed a generator purchase agreement with Wistron, which the prospectus describes as a manufacturer of AI servers for hyperscalers such as Meta and Google, to provide 21 generators and approximately 10 MW of bridge power generation for its 24/7 operations.

Prospectus financials and backlog: 2025 revenue $183.1 million (+42.5%), with power system sales product revenues $90,138 thousand (+67.0%); Q1 2026 revenue $31.7 million (+31.6%). Contracted Power System Sales Backlog $1,276,065 thousand at March 31, 2026 (+778.6% YoY) and $1,183,072 thousand at December 31, 2025 (+419.7%); substantially all of the growth came from contracts with data center customers, predominantly in Texas. Remaining performance obligations at March 31, 2026 totaled $1,376,513 thousand, of which $335,800 thousand in the remainder of 2026 and $864,523 thousand in 2027; at that time ERock expected to execute the backlog over approximately three years. Data center activity was not a significant contributor to 2025 product revenue growth; data center demand in 2025 showed up in backlog rather than revenue because of project timing.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $183.1 million (+42.5%); backlog $1,276,065 thousand at March 31, 2026 (+778.6%); RPO $1,376,513 thousand ($864,523 thousand in 2027)

quarterly_data.signal: Assembly and supply (prospectus): ERock historically used a third party to assemble its power systems and in 2025 began assembling them internally at its Titan facility in Houston, and says this shift will increase general and administrative expenses and capital expenditures and decrease margins over the near term. The RockBlock scales in 0.5 MW increments from 1.5 MW to 3.5 MW per unit. Pre-configuring and kitting key generator components reduced installation costs by 20%. Over 2,000 units are deployed across approximately 400 sites; systems have been assembled and delivered in as little as six months, with full commissioning typically 12 to 18 months from contract signing. Engine components and other products for generators, transformers and switchgear are bought under agreements that generally carry fixed volume commitments at fixed prices and multi-year terms; some long-term supply agreements include prepayment obligations, and some components are sole-sourced. A take-or-pay agreement for natural gas generators with a single vendor (spend $32.5 million in 2024 and $0.3 million in 2025) expired in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: in-house assembly at Titan since 2025; RockBlock 1.5 MW to 3.5 MW per unit; installation costs -20%; over 2,000 units at ~400 sites; take-or-pay generator purchases $32.5 million (2024)
